title: Seven Weekend Getaways From Delhi You Can Reach by Bus
excerpt: No flight, no car, no problem: Rishikesh, Jaipur, Agra, Mussoorie, Jim Corbett, Dehradun and Lansdowne are all within 290 km of Delhi and reachable by bus for a Friday-to-Sunday escape.
body:
• Seven of North India's most popular weekend destinations — from Rishikesh and Jaipur to Jim Corbett and Lansdowne — sit within 180 to 290 km of Delhi, all reachable by regular bus services.
  • The list mixes adventure (Rishikesh river rafting), heritage (Jaipur, Agra) and wildlife (Jim Corbett safaris), with suggested stays of one to two nights.
  • Quieter alternatives like Lansdowne and Dehradun offer the Himalayan foothills without Mussoorie's crowds.
  • Corbett safaris require advance planning, since zones, timings and availability vary by season.

Leave Friday, Back Sunday — No Car Required

Delhi's greatest travel advantage is distance. Some of North India's most-visited weekend destinations sit within a manageable road journey of 180 to 290 km, and a growing number of travellers are discovering that a bus — not a self-drive car or a short-haul flight — is the most practical way to get there. Leave on Friday evening, return on Sunday, and the entire trip fits inside a weekend.

The Indian Express's roundup of bus-accessible escapes covers hill towns, heritage cities, a national park and riverside retreats. Here is the shortlist, with what to actually do at each stop.

The Classics: Rishikesh, Jaipur, Agra

Rishikesh (200–240 km) remains Delhi's most versatile weekend option. Set along the Ganga in the Himalayan foothills, it packs river rafting, riverside cafés, yoga and ashrams, and the evening Ganga Aarti into one compact town. Walk the ghats, cross the Ram Jhula and Lakshman Jhula areas, or simply spend an afternoon by the river. One to two nights is ideal.

Jaipur (230–280 km) suits travellers who want a packed weekend without heading into the hills. The Pink City's forts, palaces, bazaars and food scene fill a two-day itinerary easily: Amber Fort, the City Palace and Hawa Mahal by day, the old city's markets and Rajasthani thalis by evening. Plan for one to two nights.

Agra (180–230 km) is the shortest hop and the most heritage-dense. The Taj Mahal around sunrise is the obvious anchor, but Agra Fort and the city's Mughal-era monuments — plus its street food — justify a full day. One night is enough.

The Hills: Mussoorie, Dehradun, Lansdowne

Mussoorie (220–290 km) is the familiar hill-station answer: mountain views, Mall Road walks, cafés, Kempty Falls and the quieter lanes of Landour, with viewpoints over the Doon Valley. Two nights lets you settle in rather than rush.

Dehradun (about 210 km) works as the less hectic alternative — the foothills without Mussoorie's weekend crowds. Visit Robber's Cave, work through the city's café and market scene, or use it as a base for a quick excursion up to Mussoorie itself. One to two nights.

Lansdowne (about 260 km) is the sleeper pick for travellers who actively want to avoid crowds. A quieter Himalayan foothill town with forested walks, local viewpoints and temples, it rewards the slow weekend: leisurely walks and time spent simply in the surroundings. Two nights.

The Wild Card: Jim Corbett

Jim Corbett National Park (210–260 km) is the one choice on the list that is about neither hills nor heritage. India's oldest national park offers a genuine wildlife weekend — safaris through forest landscape, resort stays on the park's edge — within bus range of Delhi. The one caveat is planning: safari zones, timings and availability vary, so book the safari portion of the trip well in advance. Two nights is the sweet spot.

A Note for Diaspora Travellers

This list is particularly useful for NRIs visiting Delhi with family. Without a car — and often without the appetite to drive in NCR traffic — a weekend trip can feel logistically daunting. Regular intercity buses to all seven destinations remove that barrier, and the one-to-two-night format fits neatly into a typical India visit's calendar. For families travelling in the cooler months, the hill options are at their best from October through March, while Corbett's safari season rewards advance booking regardless of when you go.
